content: 1. Ciprofloxacin Interaction: Pretomanid significantly inhibits OAT3 in vitro. This may increase the risk of adverse effects when co-administered with OAT3 substrates. Close monitoring is recommended, and dosage adjustments for OAT3 substrates should be considered. 2. Clavulanate and Pretomanid: Co-administration may increase the toxicity of either drug. Alternative therapies should be considered due to the risk of hepatotoxicity associated with pretomanid. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 3. Clobazam Interaction: Clobazam increases pretomanid levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as pretomanid is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. 4. Conjugated Estrogens: Pretomanid increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 5. Dabigatran Interaction: Pretomanid increases dabigatran levels. Use caution and monitor for drug-related adverse effects, especially with sensitive P-gp substrates. 6. Dabrafenib Interaction: Dabrafenib decreases pretomanid levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Danazol Interaction: Co-administration with pretomanid increases the toxicity of both drugs. Avoid or use alternative therapies. 8. Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to pretomanid’s hepatotoxicity risk. 9. Digoxin Interaction: Pretomanid increases digoxin levels. Use caution and monitor closely, especially with sensitive OATP1B3 or P-gp substrates. 10. Efavirenz Interaction: Efavirenz decreases pretomanid levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Erythromycin (Base, Ethylsuccinate, Lactobionate, Stearate): Pretomanid increases erythromycin levels, and co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Eslicarbazepine Acetate Interaction: Eslicarbazepine decreases pretomanid levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Etravirine Interaction: Etravirine decreases pretomanid levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Famotidine Interaction: Pretomanid increases famotidine levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 15. Fexofenadine Interaction: Pretomanid increases fexofenadine levels. Use caution and monitor closely, especially with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. 16. Floxuridine Interaction: Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 17. Fluoxymesterone Interaction: Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Flutamide Interaction: Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 19. Fluvastatin Interaction: Pretomanid increases fluvastatin levels. Use caution and monitor closely, especially with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. 20. Fosphenytoin Interaction: Fosphenytoin decreases pretomanid levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Furosemide Interaction: Pretomanid increases furosemide levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 22. Ganciclovir Interaction: Pretomanid increases ganciclovir levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 23. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir Interaction: Pretomanid increases the levels of these drugs. Use caution and monitor closely, especially with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. 24. Glyburide Interaction: Pretomanid increases glyburide levels. Use caution and monitor closely, especially with sensitive BCRP substrates. 25. Hydralazine Interaction: Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Ibuprofen Interaction: Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 27. Imatinib Interaction: Pretomanid increases imatinib levels. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration increases toxicity; avoid or use alternative drugs. 28. Indomethacin Interaction: Pretomanid increases indomethacin levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 29. Infliximab Interaction: Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Interferon Alfa-2b, Beta-1a, Beta-1b: Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Isoniazid Interaction: Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 32. Ivosidenib Interaction: Ivosidenib decreases pretomanid levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Ketoconazole Interaction: Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Letermovir Interaction: Pretomanid increases letermovir levels. Use caution and monitor closely, especially with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. 35. Levoketoconazole Interaction: Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Levonorgestrel (Oral): Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Levonorgestrel/Ethinyl Estradiol/Ferrous Bisglycinate: Co-administration increases toxicity. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 38. Levothyroxine Interaction: Pretomanid increases levothyroxine levels. Use caution and monitor closely, especially with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. 39. Lorlatinib Interaction: Lorlatinib decreases pretomanid levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
